chapter: New York, Dallas and Kansas City
title: Bingie Madison and the Tango Palace
summary: He explains taxi dances and tells Bingie Madison's story of being hoisted by the ankle on a stage rope with Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, a taxi dance is similar to what happened in New Orleans at the La Vida. The customers used to come in, mostly men, the girls are up there to dance with them, they're up there on one side, they get a roll of tickets and they go ahead and dance. And the musicians are up there -- most musicians that are playing in the taxi dance have come from famous bands. Bingie Madison was with Louis Armstrong for a number of years himself. The story about Bingie that always was a great story is Louis was playing at --
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
what's the name of that theater in Chicago -- The Regal?
There was a Regal in Chicago, yeh.

A Chicago theater, so Bingie is at that time, when those curtains -- they lower the curtains, or lift the curtains up, they went by ropes and Bingie was standing right in the center of some ropes and when the band was getting ready to go on, everybody was in their place and they lift up the curtains, and Bingie was hung by his ankle up there, going up there with the rope.

So they had to lower that down to save Bingie. So I heard about the story but I didn't know Bingie until I went to sit in over there, the Tango Palace, and I saw this fellow and we're talking about Louis Armstrong when he was there. I wasn't with him then, you know, but Bingie was, had been, and he was the band leader there at the Tango Palace. He told me the story himself, about his ankle.
